ops.title: Prove the fix over the REAL test body, not a reconstruction
ops.imperative: The m1 harness proves the two candidate expectations apart by reconstructing the six comparisons. That is one step short of what the handoff asks: show the corrected expectation is what the implementation returns under a simulated ntpath. Execute the actual test function from tests/test_spine_rail.py twice -- once with the three comparison lines textually reverted to the platform-inherited form, once as it stands -- under a `normcase` that FOLDS, and again under the host's identity `normcase`. Assert the substitution applied before trusting the pre-fix run, so a silently-matched-nothing revert cannot read as a passing guard. The pre-fix body must FAIL under the fold and PASS on the host; the post-fix body must PASS under both.

preconditions.statement: the fix is in tree and both target test files are green

postconditions.statement: the real test body fails pre-fix under a folding normcase and passes post-fix, while both pass under the host's identity normcase

check.command: cd /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills/.worktrees/cleanup-f-derive-worktree && env -u SPINE_FILE -u SPINE_SESSION -u SPINE_PARENT py .agent-work/cleanup-f-derive-worktree/evidence/g1-windows-testbody-sim.py

constraints: The harness lives under .agent-work/ (local-only evidence), never in tests/.
It must assert its own textual revert applied -- a check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed.
